note: Question index for diffing and authoring. Stems restated in our own wording; the mathematics is exact. No solution content from the source book appears in this file, by policy.

chapter.section_label_conflict: Every question in this chapter is filed by the book under SHORT ANSWER at 4 marks (banner 2 x 4M = 8 M), and the book's own Maths-1B model paper places this chapter at n=13 and n=14 in Section II (SAQ). Our bank holds all 15 of its rows for this unit as LAQ at 8 marks. Recorded here as the book prints it; the marks decision is the founder's.

questions.stem: Show that the product of the perpendicular distances from a point (α, β) to the pair of straight lines ax² + 2hxy + by² = 0 is |aα² + 2hαβ + bβ²| / √((a − b)² + 4h²).
questions.notes: Star prefix sits in the binding fold on p.163. Two full stars are legible plus a partial glyph consistent with a third; recorded conservatively as 2 and it is probably 3. Re-photograph the left gutter of scan 30 to settle it. Does not affect the diff.

questions.stem: If ax² + 2hxy + by² = 0 represents a pair of straight lines, show that the angle θ between the two lines is given by cos θ = ±(a + b) / √((a − b)² + 4h²).
Show that the area of the triangle formed by the pair of lines ax² + 2hxy + by² = 0 and the line lx + my + n = 0 is n²√(h² − ab) / |am² − 2hlm + bl²| square units.

If ax² + 2hxy + by² = 0 represents a pair of distinct (that is, intersecting) lines, show that the combined equation of the pair of bisectors of the angles between those lines is h(x² − y²) = (a − b)xy.

If S ≡ ax² + 2hxy + by² + 2gx + 2fy + c = 0 represents a pair of parallel straight lines, show that (i) h² = ab, (ii) af² = bg², and (iii) the distance between the parallel lines is 2√((g² − ac)/(a(a + b))) = 2√((f² − bc)/(b(a + b))).
questions.notes: Three parts under one instruction and one setup, so kept as ONE object. The printed stem joins the two distance forms with "="; both are equal once af² = bg² is established, so this is a phrasing choice, not an error.

questions.stem: If the second degree equation S ≡ ax² + 2hxy + by² + 2gx + 2fy + c = 0 in the two variables x and y represents a pair of straight lines, show that (i) abc + 2fgh − af² − bg² − ch² = 0 and (ii) h² ≥ ab, g² ≥ ac and f² ≥ bc.
questions.notes: Two parts under one instruction and one setup, so kept as ONE object.

questions.stem: Show that the product of the perpendicular distances from the origin to the pair of straight lines represented by ax² + 2hxy + by² + 2gx + 2fy + c = 0 is |c| / √((a − b)² + 4h²).
questions.notes: The scan trims the left margin of p.166 (the page-number box reads "66" with its left edge cut), so a star could be lost outside the frame. One star is legible; recorded as 1, could be 2 or 3.

questions.stem: Find the values of k for which the lines joining the origin to the points of intersection of the curve 2x² − 2xy + 3y² + 2x − y − 1 = 0 and the line x + 2y = k are mutually perpendicular.
Find the angle between the lines joining the origin to the points of intersection of the curve x² + 2xy + y² + 2x + 2y − 5 = 0 and the line 3x − y + 1 = 0.
questions.notes: Left margin of p.167 is clean, so 2 stars is certain.

questions.stem: Show that the lines joining the origin to the points of intersection of the curve x² − xy + y² + 3x + 3y − 2 = 0 and the straight line x − y − √2 = 0 are mutually perpendicular.
Find the condition for the lines joining the origin to the points of intersection of the circle x² + y² = a² and the line lx + my = 1 to coincide.
Find the condition for the chord lx + my = 1 of the circle x² + y² = a² to subtend a right angle at the origin.

Find the equation of the pair of lines joining the origin to the points of intersection of the curve 7x² − 4xy + 8y² + 2x − 4y − 8 = 0 with the straight line 3x − y = 2, and find the angle between those lines.
Find the centroid and the area of the triangle formed by the lines 12x² − 20xy + 7y² = 0 and 2x − 3y + 4 = 0.
questions.notes: The parent number 14 carries no star; each roman sub-part carries one. The two sub-parts are separate problems with different line pairs, so they are emitted as separate objects.

questions.stem: Find the centroid and the area of the triangle formed by the lines 2y² − xy − 6x² = 0 and x + y + 4 = 0.
questions.notes: See saq14i. The parent number 14 carries no star; this sub-part carries one.

questions.stem: Show that the lines represented by (lx + my)² − 3(mx − ly)² = 0 together with the line lx + my + n = 0 form an equilateral triangle whose area is n² / (√3(l² + m²)) square units.
questions.notes: No star on number 15 and none on either sub-part; the margin is clean, so 0 is certain. Printed "equllateral" for "equilateral".

questions.stem: Show that the lines (x + 2a)² − 3y² = 0 and x = a form an equilateral triangle, and find the area of that triangle.
questions.notes: A specific numeric case with its own setup, separate from saq15i, so emitted as its own object. Printed "follwoing" for "following".

questions.stem: Show that the equation 2x² − 13xy − 7y² + x + 23y − 6 = 0 represents a pair of straight lines. Also find the angle between them and the coordinates of the point of intersection of the lines.
questions.notes: Left margin of p.172 is clean, so 1 star is certain.

questions.stem: Show that the pair of lines 6x² − 5xy − 6y² = 0 and the pair 6x² − 5xy − 6y² + x + 5y − 1 = 0 form a square.
questions.notes: Stem read in full on p.172. The worked solution is on printed p.173, which is missing from the scan — the loss is solution content only, which we do not want. The parent number 17 carries no star; each sub-part carries one.

questions.stem: Show that the pair of lines 3x² + 8xy − 3y² = 0 and the pair 3x² + 8xy − 3y² + 2x − 4y − 1 = 0 form a square.
questions.notes: Stem read in full on p.172, so nothing of this question is lost. Its solution starts on the missing p.173 and finishes on p.174; solution content only. Numbering runs 17 to 18 unbroken across the gap.

questions.stem: Prove that the equation 3x² + 7xy + 2y² + 5x + 5y + 2 = 0 represents a pair of straight lines, and find the coordinates of their point of intersection.
questions.notes: Printed "resents a pair of straight lines" — the first three letters of "represents" are dropped. Last question of the chapter; the chapter closes with the *** end marker on p.174.
